control_device_fabrication: Systematic parameter adjustments underlie the fabrication of a perovskite cell that was refined and produced, capturing how controlled conditions influence a PCE of 17.229%, FF of 84.839%, Voc of 0.98662 V, and Jsc of 20.583 mA/cm². The perovskite solution (1.73 mol/L) was made according to the composition of Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79I2.9Br0.1 in a mixed solvent of DMF/DMSO. The optimal SAM was prepared by using Me-4PACz (0.33 mg/mL).The sample of Me-4PACz was fabricated with a concentration of 0.33 mg/mL. To fabricate high-quality perovskite films, MACl (20.0 mg/mL) was added to the perovskite precursor solution. The as prepared perovskite precursor was spin-coated onto the substrates at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s, respectively. The film was quickly washed with 160 µL CB at 6 s during spin-coating. The perovskite sample was subsequently annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
target_device_fabrication: This work arises from meticulous parameter optimization, where a perovskite solar device was formulated, reflecting a PCE of 18.178%, with an FF of 84.608%, Voc of 0.97906 V, and Jsc of 21.945 mA/cm². The Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79I2.9Br0.1 perovskite film was prepared with a concentration of 1.73 mol/L. Incorporating Me-4PACz (0.33 mg/mL) as a SAM was critical to adjust interfacial energy levels and refine the perovskite interface. Add MACl (10.0 mg/mL) as an additive was essential for stabilizing the perovskite structure. The perovskite solution was deposited on substrate by two consecutive spin-coating steps of 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s, respectively. At the 6 s before the end of the progress, 160 µL CB was evenly dripped onto the substrate. Then the films were annealed at 110 °C for 25 min to form the perovskite layer.
